title: Apparent Fridge-Freezer Cyberattacks Hit Grocery Stores Across Europe
meta_title: European Grocery Store Fridges Hit by Apparent Cyberattacks
meta_description: Grocery stores in Belgium, Luxembourg, and Sweden suffered unexpected temperature spikes in fridges and freezers, ruining food in a wave of apparent hacks.
discover_titles: European Grocery Stores Hit by Apparent Fridge Hacks
Apparent Cyberattacks Ruin Food in European Supermarkets
Fridge and Freezer Temperature Spikes Hit European Chains
spot: Grocery store chains in at least three European countries reported unexpected temperature spikes in refrigerators and freezers on Monday, spoiling food in the second wave of similar incidents in less than a month raising concerns over interlinked infrastructure security.
content_html:
Key Developments

Grocery retailers across Europe faced severe operational disruptions early Monday as refrigerators and freezers experienced sudden, unexpected temperature spikes that ruined stored food. Netherlands-based food retailer Ahold Delhaize and Colruyt in Belgium reported that an overnight IT incident caused cooling units in dozens of stores across Belgium and Luxembourg to soar in temperature.

Simultaneously, Swedish chains ICA and Coop reported similar spikes, with at least one outlet explicitly pointing to a cyberattack, according to Reuters. Stephan Moelans, CEO of Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel, stated that a cyberattack was responsible after the evaporator units of refrigerators and freezers were switched into defrost mode. Technicians were mobilized to disconnect affected units from the network.

These disruptions echo a similar incident from less than three weeks prior, when French supermarket chains E. Leclerc, Intermarché, and Cooperative U reported a cyberattack that pushed refrigerator temperatures as high as 122 degrees Fahrenheit across hundreds of outlets.

Key Takeaways

  • Multiple Countries Affected: Chains in Belgium, Luxembourg, and Sweden reported soaring temperatures in refrigeration units on Monday.
  • Defrost Mode Triggered: Sabcobel confirmed that attackers switched fridge and freezer evaporators into defrost mode, necessitating emergency manual disconnections.
  • Growing Security Concerns: The incidents follow a similar wave of French supermarket cyberattacks less than three weeks ago, highlighting vulnerabilities in interlinked infrastructure.

Why It Matters

The repeated incidents highlight growing cybersecurity vulnerabilities within modern, interlinked commercial infrastructure. As grocery chains rely increasingly on networked refrigeration systems for centralized temperature management, malicious interference can quickly lead to widespread food spoilage, financial losses, and significant operational challenges for major European retailers requiring costly physical and digital security upgrades.
